items.title: PBZ format specification, version 0.5
items.text:
Status: draft. Format 0.5 is the draft that format 1.0 will come from. Some rules can still change before 1.0.

A PBZ store holds per-base and binned genomic data in Zarr v3. It opens as one Xarray Dataset with xarray.open_zarr, with no PBZ code.

The words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY have the meanings of RFC 2119.

items.title: Example
items.text:
example.pbz/
  zarr.json                                             root group
  contig_id       (contig)                              ["chr1", "chr2"]
  contig_length   (contig)                              [1500, 2200]
  sample          (sample)                              ["s1", "s2", "s3"]
  threshold       (threshold)                           [5, 10]
  depth           (position, sample)                    shape [3700, 3]
  callable        (position, sample, threshold)         shape [3700, 3, 2]
  coverage        (bin_1000, sample)                    shape [5, 3]
  mean_depth      (sample)                              shape [3]

Each entry other than zarr.json is a Zarr v3 array that is a direct child of the root. The names contig_id, contig_length and contig are fixed. The other names are examples.

items.title: Root group
items.text:
The root is a Zarr v3 group. Its attributes MUST contain:

Attribute Value zarr_conventions A list that contains exactly one entry with "uuid": "d5bd7bea-0388-4e0a-9844-707c034e9add". pbz:version The string "0.5".

The UUID identifies PBZ. The name field of the entry is for display only.

The root MAY have other attributes. The Xarray coordinates attribute has no PBZ meaning. Writers MAY write it. Readers MUST NOT need it.

All arrays are direct children of the root. Readers ignore child groups.

items.title: Reference
items.text:
The reference is the ordered list of contigs. It is stored in root arrays on the dimension contig:

Array Dtype Rule contig_id string MUST exist. Names are unique and not empty. contig_length integer MUST exist. One length for each name, 0 or more. contig_md5 string MAY exist. One checksum for each name.

Index i of each array refers to the same contig. The order of the arrays is the order of the contigs on the genomic dimensions. Each length, and the sum of all lengths, MUST fit in a signed 64-bit integer.

The reference does not change after a store is made.

items.title: Dimensions and genomic geometry
items.text:
Each array that is not a scalar MUST have dimension_names, with one name for each axis. The names are not empty and are all different. All arrays that use a dimension name MUST agree on its length.

There are two kinds of genomic dimension:

Name Length Rows position sum of L_i Each base of each contig, in reference order. bin_N sum of ceil(L_i / N) The bins of N bases of each contig, in reference order.

L_i is the length of contig i. N is a positive integer with no leading zeros (bin_1000, not bin_01000). Other names that start with bin_ are not allowed.

Coordinates are 0-based and half-open. Bins start again at 0 in each contig. Bin k of a contig covers [k * N, min((k + 1) * N, L_i)), so the last bin of a contig can be short. A reader finds the contig of a row from the prefix sums of contig_length.

A track is an array with a genomic dimension. A track MUST have exactly one genomic dimension, and it MUST be the first dimension. Any number of other dimensions can follow.

A store MUST NOT have an array named position or bin_N. The row coordinates come from the reference only.

items.title: Labels and other arrays
items.text:
Each dimension that is not genomic and is not contig MUST have a 1D array with the same name and the same length. Its values are the labels of that dimension. Labels are strings or numbers, unique and not missing. For example, sample holds the sample names.

Other root arrays without a genomic dimension, such as mean_depth(sample) or a scalar, are allowed. Their values can repeat.

All arrays share one namespace, so a track cannot have the name of a dimension or a label array.

items.title: Values and user metadata
items.text:
Zarr owns the dtype, the shape, the chunks, the shards and the codecs of each array. PBZ adds no rules for them. A reader that cannot decode an array MUST report that array as unsupported. It MUST NOT read it as other data.

The Zarr fill_value is the value of positions with no data. The optional array attribute _FillValue declares a value that means "missing". It has the Xarray meaning:

  • For a float array, _FillValue is the base64 text of the little-endian 8-byte float, the form that Xarray writes. A JSON number is not allowed.
  • For an integer array, _FillValue is a JSON integer.
  • A bool array has no _FillValue.

Without _FillValue, 0 and false are ordinary values. The pbzarr writers use NaN for floats and the largest value of the dtype for integers.

Arrays MAY have other attributes, for example description or units. They have no PBZ meaning.

items.title: Consolidated metadata
items.text: A writer SHOULD put consolidated metadata in the root zarr.json when it finishes a write. This is the inline form of zarr-python v3: the attribute consolidated_metadata holds the zarr.json of each child, by path. The arrays are always the authority. A writer that changes the arrays MUST update or remove the consolidated metadata.

items.title: Zip stores
items.text: A store can be a single zip file. The zip file holds the complete store at its root, so the root zarr.json is the entry zarr.json. Writers SHOULD use Zip64, store each entry with no zip compression, and include consolidated metadata. A zip store is read-only.

items.title: Versions
items.text:
A reader MUST check the UUID and pbz:version before it reads any array:

  • A missing UUID, or a pbz:version that is missing or not a string, is an invalid store.
  • A version that the reader does not know is an unsupported version. The reader MUST NOT read it as format 0.5.
  • Format 0.4 used the UUID b7e3c1a2-5f4d-4e8a-9c1b-2d3e4f5a6b7c, with one group for each track. It is not described here. Readers report it as a legacy format.

The format version is not the version of the pbzarr packages.

items.title: Validation
items.text:
• root-attributes.schema.json is a JSON Schema for the root attributes.
  • CONFORMANCE.md has numbered rules and the valid and invalid example stores.
  • examples.py makes the example stores.
  • pbz validate STORE checks a store against these rules.

items.title: Python API
items.text: These are the public names of the pbzarr package. The text comes from the docstrings.

items.title: pbzarr.open
items.text:
open(source: PathLike, *, tracks: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, chunks: Chunks | Literal[STORED_CHUNKS] = _STORED_CHUNKS, storage_options: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> xr.Dataset

Open a PBZ store as one xr.Dataset.

Every array carries the 0-d reference coordinate. tracks= limits the data variables and keeps the reference and label coordinates. By default each track is a Dask array. A track whose first dimension is genomic gets Dask chunks of about 128 MiB: whole inner chunks along positions that do not split a shard, and all columns when they fit (else whole shards of columns). Such tracks that share an inner chunk and shard grid take the smallest of their Dask chunks, so they align. Other arrays are chunked by their stored shard (or chunk) shape. chunks=None gives lazy NumPy-backed arrays, and any other value goes to xr.open_zarr. The Dataset is a snapshot: a change in memory does not reach the store. A missing local store raises FileNotFoundError, and an unknown track name raises ValueError.

items.title: pbzarr.create
items.text:
create(destination: PathLike, *, reference: Mapping[str, int], storage_options: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> xr.Dataset

Create an empty PBZ store and return it opened.

Use it to make a store for write. The import functions do not need it: they create the store from the source headers. reference is the ordered mapping of contig name to length that every track shares. The destination must be a local path that does not exist. Remote stores are not supported yet, so storage_options must be None.

items.title: pbzarr.write
items.text:
write(target: PathLike | Dataset, variables: Mapping[str, DataArray], *, encoding: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None, storage_options: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> xr.Dataset

Add new variables to a store and return the store reopened.

target is a path, a URL, or a Dataset from open (its encoding["source"] names the store). variables maps names to xr.DataArray values; an xr.Dataset is such a mapping. The checks use the store metadata of now. A genomic dimension (position or bin_N) must come first and span the reference. Shared non-genomic dimensions must match the store's labels. write never changes an existing variable, and the Dataset passed as target does not change. If the write fails, the arrays it created are removed; it is not atomic against a crash.

A new variable whose first dimension is position and that has 1 or 2 dimensions gets the import layout: inner chunks of 65,536 positions (and 1 column), shards of 1,024 inner chunks (and up to 16 columns), and Blosc zstd level 5 with shuffle. A shard is capped at the variable length rounded up to whole inner chunks, and at the variable width. When encoding= for the variable gives chunks, shards, compressors, serializer or filters, xarray chooses the layout instead. A Dask-backed value with the import layout is rechunked to whole shards, and each write task holds one shard: a shard of 16 int32 columns is 4 GiB.

items.title: pbzarr.region
items.text:
region(obj: T, query: RegionLike, *, reference: Reference | None = None) -> T

A view of one locus of a whole-genome DataArray or Dataset.

Every genomic dimension present (position and each bin_N) is sliced to the locus, and variables with no genomic dimension pass through. The view carries the 0-d coordinates region_contig, region_start and region_end. With position, it also carries a numeric pos coordinate and "contig:pos" labels as the position coordinate. Positions are 0-based and contig-local, like region_start.

items.title: pbzarr.reduce_regions
items.text:
reduce_regions(obj: T, intervals: Intervals, reducer: Reducer, /, *, reference: Reference | None = None, q: float | Sequence[float] | None = None, by: str | Sequence[str] | None = None, ddof: int | None = None, skipna: bool | None = None) -> T

One statistic per interval, along position.

obj is a whole-genome DataArray or Dataset. The result has the same type, with a region dimension in place of position. Row i of the result is interval i of the input, and intervals may overlap. The result carries region_contig, region_start and region_end.

reducer is one of sum, mean, min, max, count, std, var, median, quantile (needs q=) or summit (needs by=). ddof= applies to std and var. skipna= (default True) ignores NaN values.

On a Dataset, variables without a genomic dimension pass through unchanged, and variables on a bin_N dimension are left out with a warning. reference= overrides the reference coordinate, or supplies it when obj has none. The result carries the reference that was used.

items.title: pbzarr.interval_mask
items.text:
interval_mask(obj: DataArray | Dataset, intervals: Intervals, /, *, reference: Reference | None = None) -> xr.DataArray

A lazy bool DataArray over position: True inside any interval.

obj is a whole-genome DataArray or Dataset with a position dimension. intervals takes the forms of reduce_regions; they are 0-based and half-open, and they may overlap. The mask is a Dask array with the position chunks of obj, and it carries the reference that was used.

items.title: Limits of the crates.io build
items.text:
• The importers (d4, bigWig, BED, BAM and CRAM) are in the pbzarr-readers crate, which is not on crates.io yet. Use the pbz command or the Python package to import files.
  • This repository builds against a patched zarrs. A build from crates.io uses upstream zarrs, where a partial read of an array that uses the transpose codec fails. The default layout does not use transpose.
